metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent took one screenshot, correctly identified that Google Play DRM content cannot be played in VLC, and declared the task infeasible. The VLC background cone was visible in the screenshot. Evaluator awarded full score.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can inspect visual desktop state; the VLC background cone is visible and VLC preferences are accessible.
metadata.explanation: Task asks user to disable the background cone logo in VLC via Tools > Preferences > Interface > Show cone icon in the main interface. Evaluator kills VLC (forces config save), reads ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc and checks qt-bgcone=0. Default is 1 (enabled — visible in screenshot), so initial state does not pass. Task directly builds on the trajectory evidence (cone was seen in screenshot).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_vlc_config) correctly reads ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc on Linux, which is the right file containing qt-bgcone.

Metric (check_qt_bgcone) correctly defaults qt_bgcone to '1' (VLC default) and scans all config lines for 'qt-bgcone=', taking the last match — this handles both commented defaults and explicit user-set values correctly.

Postconfig kills VLC before reading config, which forces VLC to flush and save its settings to disk. The 2-second sleep provides adequate settling time. This is the correct pattern for VLC config evaluation.
Expected value 'expected_qt_bgcone': '0' correctly represents cone hidden/disabled, matching the instruction 'hide the background cone logo'.

Parameter handling is correct: expected.type='rule' means get_rule returns the rules dict directly; check_qt_bgcone(actual_config_path, rule) accesses rule['expected_qt_bgcone'] directly without wrapping.
Negative control resistance is sound: initial state has qt-bgcone=1 (default), so the initial state does not pass the check.
Full instruction coverage: single requirement (hide cone) is fully and exclusively verified by the evaluator.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: check_qt_bgcone does not skip comment lines (e.g., '#qt-bgcone=1'), so a commented default could temporarily set the scanned value. However, since the function takes the last match and VLC always writes explicit settings after commented defaults, this does not affect correctness in practice. Consider adding a comment-skip guard (if line.lstrip().startswith('#'): continue) for robustness.
